_readme: THE RULE THESE NUMBERS SERVE. 14-ai-design.md: the builder's auto-generate
'runs live from the player's collection (pool restricted to owned cards),
then reports which suggested cards the player is missing'. Every suggestion
below is drawn from what the account owns; anything it would have suggested
and cannot is reported separately as something to craft.
WHY WEIGHTS AND NOT A HEURISTIC IN CODE. A suggestion the player disagrees
with is a suggestion they need to be able to argue with, and a number in a
file is arguable. It also means the ranking can be re-tuned after a human
playtest without touching a line of TypeScript — which is the one lever the
balance work has been waiting on.
THE SCORE. Every candidate is scored as the weighted sum of five terms, and
the largest term is what the suggestion says out loud. That is the whole
reason the terms are separate rather than one blended number: a suggestion
that cannot explain itself is one nobody can act on.

_note: curve      — how many cards short of TARGET_CURVE this card's cost bucket
is. The single most useful signal for a half-built deck, and
the highest weight for that reason.
tag        — how often this faction's own targeting filters name a tag the
card carries. Derived by payoffTags() from the card data, so
it needs no per-faction archetype list to maintain.
synergy    — how many cards ALREADY in the draft share a tag with it. This
is what makes suggestions converge on an archetype instead of
recommending thirty unrelated good cards.
current    — a small nudge toward the leader's Primary Current, which is
what keeps Confluences and Resonance reachable.
resonance  — a larger nudge, but only for a deck that is already pure: a
pure deck is seven cards from Perfect Resonance and every
off-Current card throws that away.
`show` is how many suggestions the panel offers at once. Small on purpose:
a list of twenty is a second card pool, and the player already has one.
`craftTargets` is how many cards it will name that it would have suggested
if you owned them. §14 requires it report them; it does not require a
shopping list as long as the pool.
`minScoreToShow` stops the panel padding itself out with cards it has no
actual reason to recommend once the good ones run out. A short honest list
beats a long one.
For a card in the list the account cannot legally run — an imported deck
code, or a card dismantled after the deck was saved — the closest owned
substitute. Closeness is scored on the same terms as a suggestion, plus a
bonus for landing in the same cost bucket, because a replacement that
changes the curve is not a replacement.
`sameCostBonus` is deliberately large: the whole point of a replacement is
that the deck keeps its shape.
